capitals.note: Askia Nuh 'established his capital at Lulami'; the page gives no coordinates, so the point is Gaya (Niger), the page's southern Dendi centre, as a proxy.

rulers.name: Sonni Ali
rulers.note: Reigned 1464 to 6 November 1492 (rulers table); the infobox starts the Sonni dynasty in 1468.

rulers.name: Sonni Baru

rulers.name: Askia Muhammad I
rulers.note: 3 March 1493 to 26 August 1528 (deposed by his son Musa).

rulers.name: Askia Ishaq II
rulers.note: 9 April 1588 to 14 April 1591; defeated at Tondibi on 13 March 1591.

rulers.name: Muhammad Gao
rulers.note: From 14 April 1591; deposed ruler's brother, later murdered on the pasha's orders (Dendi Kingdom page).

rulers.name: Askia Nuh
rulers.note: 1591 to 1599; deposed by his followers in favour of Harun (Dendi Kingdom page).

region.text: the Gao heartland around the Niger bend, Cliopatria's first Songhai shape

ledger.note: c. 1435: Gao leaves the Mali Empire and Songhai begins its rise. Infobox 'Independence from Mali Empire: c. 1430s'; the lead puts a Songhai state at Gao 'since the 11th century'. 1435 is a mid-decade year chosen to match the mali-empire dossier.

region.text: Dendi, the easternmost province on the Niger under the Dendi-fari, with its fleet at Ayorou; Cliopatria's Songhai shapes stop at 1.7 E and omit it

ledger.note: 1464: Sunni Ali inherits the Niger from Dendi. At his accession Songhay already controlled the Niger basin 'from Dendi to Mema'. The page does not say when Dendi was won, so 1464 (the accession) is a bridge.

region.text: Mema, west of Timbuktu, and the Niger lands lost with it (the difference of Mali's 1463 and 1468 shapes, as in the mali-empire dossier)

ledger.note: 1460s: Mema falls to Songhai. The Sunni Ali page has the empire already controlling the Niger basin 'from Dendi to Mema' at accession (1464); the Songhai page: 'In the 1460s, Sonni Sulayman Dama attacked Méma, the Mali province west of Timbuktu.' The mali-empire dossier dates the loss to 1465 from the Mali page; the Cliopatria step comes at 1468.

1468: Sunni Ali takes Timbuktu from the Tuareg. 'He annexed Timbuktu in 1468 after the leaders of the town asked him to help overthrow the Tuaregs'; the lead: conquered 'in 1468 and 1475, respectively'. The Sunni Ali page has the Timbuktu-koi ask for protection in 1469.

1475: Sunni Ali takes Djenné. The lead dates the conquest to 1475, the Sunni Ali section says 'After a seven-year siege, he was able to starve them into surrender, incorporating the town into his empire in 1473'; the Sunni Ali page has the siege laid in 1473. 1475 follows the lead and Cliopatria's step.

minus.text: the province of Diafunu (the researcher's proxy, as in the mali-empire dossier; the pages give no location)

region.text: the northern Sahel lands between Mali's 1474 and 1475 shapes, without Diafunu

ledger.note: 1475: the Inner Niger Delta and the northern Sahel pass to Songhai in Cliopatria. The Sunni Ali page lists his conquests (Timbuktu, Massina, the Inner Niger Delta, Djenné, the Sanhaja lands of Nunu and the lands of Kunta) without years, so the year is the Cliopatria step and the mali-empire dossier's own 1475 loss, bridged here (page silent).
1493: Askia Muhammad founds the Askiya dynasty. 'Ture defeated Baru at the Battle of Anfao in April 1493 outside of Gao and took power and the title Askia.' Same state, same colour (rule 2).

region.text: the province of Diafunu (the researcher's proxy, as in the mali-empire dossier; the pages give no location)

ledger.note: 1501: Askia Muhammad takes Diafunu. In 1501 he 'sacked and captured Diafunu' after defeating Qama-fiti-Kalli. The page gives no location; Nioro du Sahel is a proxy. The mali-empire dossier has the same capture in 1502 (Mali page).

region.text: Aïr, the north-eastern limit of the empire 'from Air in the Northeast to Futa Djallon'

ledger.note: 1515: Askia Muhammad reaches Aïr. 'In 1515 saw another campaign against Agadez'; the page gives his reach 'from Air in the Northeast to Futa Djallon in Guinea' but no outcome sentence for the campaign, so the land is the researcher's reading.

region.text: the salt mines of Taghaza 'brought within the empire's boundaries'

ledger.note: Undated, under Askia Muhammad (1493-1528): 'the salt mines of Taghaza were brought within the empire's boundaries.' The page names no year or former holder; 1515 only bundles it with the Aïr step.

region.text: the western strip added to the 1497 outline by Cliopatria's 1564 shape

ledger.note: 1564: Cliopatria extends the shape west to the Senegal coast. No page opened dates it; the Songhai page says only that the empire 'extended over the current territories of Mali, Niger, Nigeria, Mauritania, Senegal' at its zenith. Bridged, page silent.

region.text: Gao, Timbuktu and Djenné, the three cities Judar Pasha sacked

ledger.note: 13 March 1591: the Moroccans meet the Songhai at Tondibi. 'On 13 March 1591, the armies met at a place called Tankondibogho, near Tondibi, just north of Gao'; Judar had reached the Niger on 28 February. Left without a month because later 1591 events in this ledger carry none.

1591: Gao and Timbuktu fall. 'The Moroccan forces under Judar Pasha defeated the Songhai under Askia Ishaq II, guaranteeing the empire's downfall'; Judar sacked Gao, then Timbuktu and Djenné (the page dates none of the sacks). The saadi-sultanate dossier dates Timbuktu to 30 May 1591.

union.text: Dendi, the easternmost province on the Niger under the Dendi-fari, with its fleet at Ayorou; Cliopatria's Songhai shapes stop at 1.7 E and omit it

region.text: the rest of the empire outside Dendi, Gao, Timbuktu and Djenné

ledger.note: 1591: the old empire dissolves into small kingdoms. 'The looting of the three cities marked the end of the Songhai Empire as an effective force in the region'; the Saadis later 'relinquished control of the region', letting it 'splinter into dozens of smaller kingdoms'. Everything outside Dendi and the three cities is read as stateless from here.

region.text: Gao, Timbuktu and Djenné, the three cities Judar Pasha sacked

ledger.note: 1591: the fighting for the Niger bend ends with the cities in Moroccan hands; the Tondibi page speaks of about a decade of sporadic fighting after, and gives no later date.
1591: the Askia court leaves Gao for Dendi. Askia Nuh 'established his capital at Lulami'; the page gives no year for the move, which follows Tondibi.
1592: Djenné passes to the Moroccans. The Tondibi page has Judar proceed to Timbuktu and Djenné without dates; 1592 is the saadi-sultanate dossier's date from another page (page silent here).

region.text: Dendi, the easternmost province on the Niger under the Dendi-fari, with its fleet at Ayorou; Cliopatria's Songhai shapes stop at 1.7 E and omit it

ledger.note: 1599: the Songhai Empire ends. The infobox gives 'Saadian invasion of the Songhai Empire: 1599'; Askia Nuh's followers depose him in favour of Harun that year, and the Askia line continues in Dendi. Cliopatria's tiny shapes run to 1608.

wars.name: Sunni Ali's conquests on the Niger
wars.outcome: Songhai takes Mema (1460s), Timbuktu (1468) and Djenné (1475, after a siege laid in 1473), and the Inner Niger Delta.
wars.note: The pages disagree on Djenné: 1473 (text), 1475 (lead); the Sunni Ali page has the siege laid in 1473.

wars.name: Songhai-Mossi wars
wars.outcome: Sunni Ali 'had to abandon this project ... to defeat an invasion by the Mossi people' in 1483. Askia Muhammad later declared jihad on the Mossi (undated on the Askia page); no land is recorded as changing hands.

wars.name: Battle of Anfao (Askia coup)
belligerents: Sonni Baru and the Sonni court
wars.outcome: Askia Muhammad (Ture) defeats Sonni Baru outside Gao in April 1493 and founds the Askiya dynasty; a change of dynasty, not of land.

wars.name: Askia Muhammad's campaigns

zones.text: the province of Diafunu (the researcher's proxy, as in the mali-empire dossier; the pages give no location)
Aïr, the north-eastern limit of the empire 'from Air in the Northeast to Futa Djallon'

wars.outcome: Diafunu captured 1501; Borgu invaded 1504 'ended in disaster'; Walata captured but not held 1504; Futa Kingi destroyed and the Kingdom of Diarra brought under the empire's sway 1512 (no location on the page); another campaign against Agadez 1515.
wars.note: Futa Kingi and Diarra are not written as ledger events because no page opened places them.

wars.name: Songhai civil wars
wars.outcome: Askia Musa deposes his father in August 1528; 'several civil wars within the empire ensured the empire's continued decline', and a war of succession after Daoud (1582) 'split it into two feuding factions'. No land is recorded as changing hands.

wars.name: Moroccan invasion of the Songhai Empire

zones.text: Gao, Timbuktu and Djenné, the three cities Judar Pasha sacked

wars.outcome: Judar Pasha, sent by Ahmad al-Mansur (the lead has the force sent in 1590, the text 1591), crosses the Niger on 28 February 1591 and defeats Askia Ishaq II at Tondibi on 13 March; Gao, Timbuktu and Djenné are sacked.

wars.name: Songhai resistance in Dendi
wars.outcome: Nuh holds out at Lulami; Mahmud ibn Zarqun's two-year war ends with his withdrawal in 1594 and death that year; a later Moroccan campaign fails and Nuh's followers depose him in 1599. No land changes hands.

certainty.note: No treaty or survey fixes any Songhai frontier: the Niger valley cities are known, the Sahelian and Saharan limits (Taghaza, Aïr, the Senegal side) are approximate throughout.

notes: Pages opened: five (budget 5). Cliopatria's 1463-1594 shapes stop at 1.7 E and so omit Dendi, which the Sunni Ali page counts in the empire at accession; every shape is unioned with Dendi (Tillabéri and Gaya). The 1475 shape holds Diafunu 26 years before the Askia page's 1501, so Diafunu is withdrawn until then (overlaps the mali-empire dossier, whose 1475 shape also lacks it: a gap-filler should hold Diafunu in Mali to 1501). The infobox gives 1,400,000 km2 for 1528 against Cliopatria 629,260 km2: not reconciled, the 1515 keyframe adds only Aïr and Taghaza. The 1564 western strip is undated on every page. End: set at 1599 (infobox) though Tondibi (1591) ended the empire's effective power; Cliopatria's 1595-1608 specks are marked wrong and the Dendi remnant needs a dendi-kingdom dossier. Not mapped for lack of a located, dated page: Futa Kingi and Diarra (1512), Kebbi, Katsina, Zaria and Kano, Walata (1504, not held), Borgu. The Saadi occupations of Taghaza (1556-57, 1586) are in the saadi-sultanate dossier; the pages here do not date them. Counterparts without dossiers: Tuareg of Timbuktu, Djenné, Sultanate of Agadez, Mossi, dendi-kingdom. Gazetteer lacks Dendi, Mema, Diafunu, Taghaza (a coordinate is used).
